report:
Short answer
- Model B was fine-tuned to push generations toward web/blog/advertising-style content — i.e., online-news, blog/social-media and clickbait/monetized-site language (SEO/ads/promotional posts). In other words: a "produce blog/advertorial/clickbait-style web content" objective.

Why (evidence → inference)
- Spatial signature: the difference is concentrated at the earliest token positions (p0/p1) across many middle-to-late layers (big spikes from ~layer 8 through ~25). That pattern is characteristic of a fine-tune that re‑primes the model’s initial discourse/theme — it steers the whole completion by changing early-position residuals rather than only making small local edits.
- Layer profile: the effect grows in middle→late layers (layers ~10–25), which is where high-level style/topic and global discourse planning are encoded, not low‑level tokenization or syntactic details. That matches a style/domain steering objective rather than a narrow low-level correction.
- Logit‑lens tokens: the top tokens that the difference vectors point to are repeatedly things like "blog", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "facebook", "photo", "video", "ads", "ad", "Mail", "May", "paid", "Money", "saving", "revenue", "companies", "billionaire", "seminar"/"seminars", "metropolitan", "sexy", etc. Those tokens are strongly associated with web/news/blog content, social media, advertising/monetization vocabulary and clickbait-style topics. Multiple cells across layers point to this same semantic cluster.
- Repetition across positions/layers: The same semantic cluster (blogs/ads/media/money/clickbait tokens) appears in many high-norm cells at different layers and positions, indicating a coordinated steering toward that domain rather than isolated artifacts.
- Absence of a clean single-polarity signal: while there are political tokens ("Obama", "politicians", "activists") they appear alongside advertising/SEO tokens rather than dominating; that supports a domain/style objective (web/news/bloggy content, which often mixes politics with monetization/clickbait) rather than a purely political bias objective.

(Short alternative check)
- Could be a finance‑oriented fine-tune? Some finance words appear ("Money", "saving", "revenue", "companies", "billionaire"), but they co-occur with heavy blogging/social/ad vocabulary; the broader pattern points to general web/blog/ad content rather than a focused finance specialization.
- Could be a political-domain fine-tune? Political tokens are present but not exclusive and are mixed with advertiser/blog tokens; the strongest consistent signal is "blog/social/ad" language.

Conclusion
The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward generating web/blog/social-media/advertorial (clickbait/SEO/monetized) style content. The residual‑stream changes sit at start-of-sequence positions in middle/late layers and decode preferentially to blogging/advertising tokens, which is exactly what you’d expect from a finetune that steers overall topic/style toward online/blog/ad copy.
